core_question: Does the source-internal nearest-two-phylogenetic-neighbour predictive benefit seen for four flavonol-related genes also extend to measured flavonol metabolite concentrations when six-bit anthocyanidin-presence identity is already known?

two_fixed_biochemical_response_groups.chemical_role: measured flavonol production branch, functional readout for source fixed flavonol-related gene expression
measured terminal anthocyanidin amount within known presence/absence identities, not an independent phenotype class

transformation.source_units: original mg/g, nonnegative finite source compound values
transformation.per_compound_feature_transform: log1p(100*x) with x measured source mg/g, not log(x) or data-selected binarization
transformation.training_scaling: for each withheld tip, variance of transformed concentration across other 46 source taxa, denominator n=46 (ddof=0); if zero, replace denominator with 1, never remove an outcome-opened compound
transformation.multiresponse_loss: mean squared scaled prediction error across all exactly three preregistered metabolites in each response group, then equal weight across all 47 withheld species
transformation.prior_expression_prediction: do NOT predict module gene expression again in the new test; source original flavonol 4-gene module practical gain +0.05613676603732491 and Holm p 0.0003 remain fixed

prediction.source_tree: same original 11genestre dated source, use exact original patristic distances and lexical-tie ordering
prediction.known_target_data: the target's six-bit anthocyanidin presence class is assumed already known; prediction does not infer class identity
prediction.baseline: mean log1p(100*compound mg/g) among all other same-presence-class tips, same as existing gene prediction source donor eligibility
prediction.nearest_two: arithmetic mean transformed compound concentrations of two nearest original-tree neighbours *within same source six-bit class*, frozen k=2
prediction.gain: (source class-wide mean scaled MSE - source nearest-two scaled MSE) / source class-wide mean scaled MSE
prediction.positive_practical_requirement: observed relative gain > 0; a positive permutation-locality P with negative net gain is NOT practical transfer

null.exchangeability: For each permutation, shuffle intact SIX-compound (3 flavonol + 3 anthocyanidin) measured concentration vectors only among taxa with identical original six-bit anthocyanidin-presence codes, preserving within-taxon metabolite covariance, zeros, and source phylogeny/taxon membership. Recompute both group losses.
null.p_value: upper-tail (1 + number of permuted gains >= observed gain)/10000
null.holm_familywise: Holm adjustment for the two original independent biochemical target families; report adjusted locality P for both.
null.decision: SUPPORTED_RETROSPECTIVE_METABOLITE_TRANSFER only if observed gain>0 AND Holm P<=0.05; else NOT_SUPPORTED_PRACTICAL_TRANSFER or NOT_SUPPORTED_LOCALITY_AFTER_MULTIPLICITY
null.unit_of_permutation: whole species chemical vector, not 47×3 features, individual pair events or nearest neighbour donor sets

secondary_descriptive.source_original_6_state_perclass_gain: report six per-class gain/MSE values for each biochemical group; do not select positive-only classes
secondary_descriptive.one_class_recipient_omissions: using original fixed neighbour donor weights and variance, omit only evaluation recipients from one class; no independent tests or refits
secondary_descriptive.zero_denominator_original_state: If an original six-bit code contains all-zero measured analytes and its class-mean MSE is exactly zero, retain all its taxa in pooled 47-tip prediction/null and record only the within-class relative gain as null (0/0); never drop or relabel zero-state taxa. This is a structural implementation clarification before any complete source biochemical outcome, not new source selection.
